label: PF Backlog 613
title: Reconciliation/360 review must include an explicit LANGUAGE CHECK (Go for new shipped/sensitive logic; Python only to extend existing; shipped/customer-visible runtime = Go)
body:
Problem: the binding RECONCILIATION block (AGENTS.md/EOS) has PRIOR DECISIONS / EXISTING PATH / ASSUMPTIONS / DIVERGENCES / OPEN QUESTIONS, but no explicit LANGUAGE CHECK line, so the Go-first rule (BI-PF-0395 enforcing BI-PF-0387/0388) is applied ad hoc - e.g. is a new file shipped logic (Go) or tooling/CI (allowed)?

Policy (config/language-rule.json): shipped_roots = core/, api/, adapters/; sensitive = core/licensing.py, core/billing.py; new modules/logic there MUST be Go (existing .py edits allowed; allow_new_python exemptions); tooling_roots (scripts/, config/, docs/, data/, test-framework/, templates/, .github/, ...) may be Python/other; dashboard/ is legacy-exempt.

Proposal: add a LANGUAGE CHECK section to the reconciliation template + the Gate-1 checklist, citing `python scripts/dev/language_rule_review.py <item>` output, and stating for each new/edited file whether it is Go-required, an allowed .py edit, or tooling. Enforce in the pre-implementation review so it is decided once, up front (as already required at take-up).

brief.problem: Reconciliation has no explicit language (Go-first) check line.
brief.what_adds: LANGUAGE CHECK section + Gate-1 citation of language_rule_review.py.
brief.why: New shipped/sensitive logic must be Go; decide once up front, not ad hoc.

objective: Make the language rule an explicit, cited section of every reconciliation/Gate-1 review.
acceptance_criteria: The reconciliation template (AGENTS.md/EOS) includes a LANGUAGE CHECK section.
Gate-1 reviews cite language_rule_review.py and classify each changed/new file (Go-required | allowed .py edit | tooling).
A check/validator flags a review missing the LANGUAGE CHECK (or the review tooling emits it by default).
